title: The Trouble with Geniuses, Part 2
coreMove: Practical intelligence turns ability into navigable action: asking clearly, reading authority, pressing respectfully, and surviving institutional friction.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a student may lose aid because no one taught the appeal script
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Langan at Reed and Montana State to teach an appeal script.

exampleSpecs.stakes: confidence may be rewarded as merit when it is partly trained status
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Oppenheimer to question confidence as merit.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a teacher may reward one family code while misreading another
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Annette Lareau's studies to interpret parent meetings.

exampleSpecs.stakes: quiet interns may miss chances because they lack the asking code
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn practical intelligence into internship practice.

exampleSpecs.stakes: some students may receive grace because they know elite codes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Oppenheimer to review unequal grace.

exampleSpecs.stakes: parents may leave without answers because deference is mistaken for agreement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply Lareau's authority research in a clinic.
